title: DataGate
problem_statement: Analytics and data engineering teams at mid-size companies (200–2,000 employees) face a critical tradeoff: overly restrictive data access creates 2–3 week analyst wait times via manual Jira/Slack workflows, while overly permissive access exposes customer PII in shared notebooks and personal cloud buckets, generating SOC 2 and GDPR audit findings. The root cause is the absence of a consistent, automated access governance layer — no structured approval routing, no time-bounded grants, and no auditable provisioning trail. As regulatory scrutiny intensifies and data team headcount grows, this ad-hoc approach becomes both a productivity bottleneck and a compliance liability that manual processes cannot scale to address.
target_users: Data analyst who frequently requests access to production datasets and is blocked by slow manual ticketing processes
Data engineer responsible for provisioning and managing database permissions across Snowflake or BigQuery environments
Security or compliance officer accountable for SOC 2 and GDPR audit readiness and maintaining access audit trails
Data or analytics manager who approves access requests and needs visibility into who has access to what datasets
IT or infrastructure administrator who manages integrations between the access portal and underlying cloud data warehouse permissions
user_stories: As a data analyst who frequently requests access to production datasets and is blocked by slow manual ticketing processes, I want to submit a self-serve access request specifying the dataset, purpose, and duration so that I receive provisioned access within hours instead of waiting 2–3 weeks for a Jira ticket to be fulfilled

As a data analyst who frequently requests access to production datasets and is blocked by slow manual ticketing processes, I want to see the real-time status of my pending access requests and estimated approval time so that I can plan my work without needing to follow up over Slack

As a data or analytics manager who approves access requests and needs visibility into who has access to what datasets, I want to receive structured approval requests with dataset sensitivity classification, requester justification, and requested duration so that I can make informed access decisions in under 15 minutes without needing additional context

As a data or analytics manager who approves access requests and needs visibility into who has access to what datasets, I want a dashboard showing all currently active access grants, their expiry dates, and the approving manager so that I can audit team-wide data access at a glance

As a security or compliance officer accountable for SOC 2 and GDPR audit readiness and maintaining access audit trails, I want an immutable, timestamped audit log recording every access request, approval decision, provisioning action, and expiry event so that I can produce a complete access history for auditors without manual reconstruction

As a security or compliance officer accountable for SOC 2 and GDPR audit readiness and maintaining access audit trails, I want automatic access expiry enforced at the Snowflake or BigQuery permission level when a time-bounded grant lapses so that no analyst retains access beyond the approved window even if manual revocation is forgotten

As a data engineer responsible for provisioning and managing database permissions across Snowflake or BigQuery environments, I want approved access requests to automatically trigger role or permission grants in the connected data warehouse via API so that I no longer need to manually execute GRANT statements or track outstanding provisioning tasks

As an IT or infrastructure administrator who manages integrations between the access portal and underlying cloud data warehouse permissions, I want to configure role-mapping rules that translate DataGate access tiers to specific Snowflake roles or BigQuery IAM bindings so that provisioning is deterministic and does not require per-request engineering intervention
acceptance_criteria: An analyst can submit an access request form capturing dataset name, business justification, requested permission level (read/write), and access duration (1 day to 90 days) in under 3 minutes with no engineering assistance

Submitted requests are automatically routed to the correct approver based on a configurable dataset-to-approver mapping; misrouted requests must be reroutable by an admin within the portal without engineering involvement

Approvers receive an email and in-app notification within 60 seconds of a request being submitted, containing dataset name, sensitivity classification, requester identity, justification, and requested duration
Upon approver approval, Snowflake or BigQuery permissions are provisioned automatically via API within 5 minutes, and the requester receives a confirmation notification with access details
Access grants expire automatically at the approved end date and time; the underlying Snowflake role grant or BigQuery IAM binding is revoked within 15 minutes of expiry with no manual action required

The audit log captures every state transition (submitted, approved, denied, provisioned, expired, manually revoked) with actor identity, timestamp, and IP address, and is exportable as a tamper-evident CSV or JSON file for auditor use
Sensitivity classification (e.g., PII, financial, internal) is assignable per dataset by a data engineer or admin and is displayed on every request and approval screen
Requests for datasets classified as PII require a secondary approval from a security or compliance officer before provisioning proceeds

The portal surfaces a read-only access inventory view showing every active grant, the grantee, dataset, permission level, approver, grant date, and expiry date, filterable by team and dataset sensitivity
Role-mapping configuration UI allows IT admins to map DataGate permission tiers to specific Snowflake roles or BigQuery IAM roles without writing code
The system sends automated email reminders to access holders 7 days and 1 day before grant expiry, with a one-click renewal request link
End-to-end request-to-provisioning time (submission to active permission) is measurable and logged per request to support SLA reporting

success_metrics.metric: Median time from access request submission to active permission provisioned
success_metrics.target: Under 4 hours for standard requests and under 24 hours for PII-classified requests

success_metrics.metric: Percentage of active data access grants with a defined expiry date and automated revocation
success_metrics.baseline: Less than 10% (most grants are indefinite and manually managed)
success_metrics.target: 100% of grants issued through DataGate have a defined expiry and automated revocation

success_metrics.metric: Audit findings related to unauthorized or unrevoked data access in SOC 2 or GDPR audits
success_metrics.baseline: 3–5 findings per audit cycle reported by security team
success_metrics.target: Zero access-governance-related audit findings in the first full audit cycle after DataGate deployment

success_metrics.metric: Data engineer time spent per week on manual permission provisioning and revocation tasks
success_metrics.baseline: Estimated 6–10 hours per week per data engineer based on pre-launch survey
success_metrics.target: Under 1 hour per week per data engineer, with remaining time limited to exception handling

success_metrics.metric: Analyst satisfaction score with the data access process (measured via post-request survey, 1–5 scale)
success_metrics.baseline: 2.1 average (measured via baseline survey before launch)
success_metrics.target: 4.0 or above within 90 days of full deployment

risks_open_questions: Risk: Snowflake and BigQuery permission APIs have rate limits and occasional downtime; a failed provisioning API call could leave an approved request in a limbo state — need a retry mechanism, dead-letter queue, and manual override fallback for admins

Risk: Dataset sensitivity classification depends on human tagging by data engineers; inconsistent or missing classifications could route PII requests through single-approver workflows — consider automated PII detection (e.g., scanning column names or metadata) as a classification assist

Open question: Should DataGate support additional data warehouses (Databricks, Redshift, Postgres RDS) in v1, or is Snowflake + BigQuery sufficient to cover 80% of the target market? Scope decision affects integration build time significantly

Risk: Approval routing rules may become stale as teams and dataset ownership change; if an approver leaves the company, requests could be orphaned — need an escalation path and fallback approver configuration

Open question: How should DataGate handle emergency break-glass access scenarios where an analyst needs immediate access outside normal approval workflows, and how is that access audited and retroactively reviewed?

Risk: If DataGate's API credentials to Snowflake or BigQuery are compromised, it represents a high-privilege attack surface — need to define credential rotation policy, least-privilege service account scoping, and secrets management integration (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault)
Open question: Should access renewal require a full re-approval cycle or allow self-renewal with manager notification for non-PII datasets? The tradeoff is compliance rigor versus analyst friction

Risk: Adoption failure if analysts find the portal slower or more cumbersome than the existing Slack-based ad-hoc requests — need to ensure the request form is completable in under 3 minutes and that the mobile-responsive design supports approvers approving on the go
out_of_scope: Data warehouse query execution, notebook environments, or BI tool integrations (DataGate provisions access only; it does not provide a query or visualization layer)
Support for on-premises databases, MySQL, SQL Server, or any data warehouse other than Snowflake and BigQuery in v1
Row-level or column-level security enforcement within the data warehouse (DataGate manages role/dataset-level grants only; column masking policies are out of scope for v1)
User identity provider management or SSO configuration (DataGate will integrate with an existing corporate IdP such as Okta or Azure AD but will not manage identity lifecycle)
Automated discovery or cataloging of datasets (DataGate assumes datasets are pre-registered in its catalog by a data engineer or admin; automated schema crawling is out of scope for v1)
Data lineage tracking or impact analysis of access grants on downstream pipelines
Billing or chargeback reporting for data access costs by team or department
Mobile native applications (the portal will be a responsive web application only)
Direct integration with Jira or ServiceNow to auto-close existing tickets when access is provisioned (migration tooling for legacy workflows is out of scope for v1)
